_about: Weather dials: bands, what each band does to the air, and wind directions. Tones colour the dial: for wind and mixing height they show the effect on pollution (red = traps it).

bands.name: Cold
bands.air: Cold air near the ground often traps smoke under a warmer layer above (an inversion).

bands.name: Cool
bands.air: Cool air near the ground often traps smoke under a warmer layer above (an inversion), worst at night and early morning.

bands.name: Hot
bands.air: Heat and strong sun turn traffic fumes into ozone in the afternoon.

bands.name: Very hot
bands.air: Heat and strong sun turn traffic fumes into ozone in the afternoon; heat itself also strains the heart and lungs.

bands.name: Dry
bands.air: Dry air lets road and building dust (PM10) lift and stay up easily.

bands.name: Humid
bands.air: Humid air helps fine particles grow and linger, which makes haze and smog worse.

bands.name: Very humid
bands.air: Humid air helps fine particles grow and linger, which makes haze and smog worse; fog can form at night.

bands.name: Calm
bands.air: Very little wind, so pollution is not being blown away and builds up near the ground.

bands.name: Light breeze
bands.air: A light breeze is moving some pollution along, but slowly.

bands.name: Gentle breeze
bands.air: A gentle breeze is moving pollution along.

bands.name: Moderate breeze
bands.air: A good breeze is helping to clear pollution.

bands.name: Strong wind
bands.air: Strong wind clears smoke but can raise dust (PM10).

bands.name: Very low lid
bands.air: The air can only mix up to about {value} m, like a low lid over the city: smoke has nowhere to go.

bands.name: Low lid
bands.air: The air mixes only up to about {value} m, so pollution stays close to the ground.

bands.name: High
bands.air: The air mixes high up (about {value} m), which thins pollution out.

explain.mixing: How high the air can mix
explain.mixing_help: The height the air near the ground can rise and mix to. Below a few hundred metres, smoke is trapped like under a lid.
explain.title: Weather in {name}

stubble.text: Wind from the north-west in October and November can carry smoke from crop-stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana.
